scenario: [LTSL.3.2] / [LTSL.3.7]: an absolute timeline coordinate is a `calendar.time` call whose arguments fold, in the `at` and the `until` positions ([LGRA.21.1]'s `time_coord ::= UNIT_LIT | postfix`), here gating a rule on `now()`, which absolute mode fixes. The control for LTSL.3.7_quoted_stamp_refused and LTSL.3.7_before_1970_refused: the same shape compiles when the coordinate is one. The folded instant, 2026-06-18T14:00:00Z as `when_ns` 1781791200000000000, is test_dstest's check. PATH PINNED: `dsc.parse`'s `ltsl_3_3_at_block` and `until` section reading a postfix, and `dsc.dstest.ltsl_3_1_coordinate` folding it through `ltim_14_3_calendar_fold`.
rules_ds:
import calendar

schema Ping scope logical:
    id: Int key

rule late:
    Ping where now() > calendar.time(2026, 6, 18)
->
    log info "late"

test "an absolute coordinate":
    inputs:
        at calendar.time(2026, 6, 18, 14, 0, 0):
            Ping id: 1
    until calendar.time(2026, 6, 18, 15, 0, 0)
    produces:
        activated late
